rv.q: This is a package that contains the very best of Christmas.
At this point, six years after its premiere, director Matthew Warchus’ production is a fast-paced, slick and moving festive treat.
Christopher Eccleston... is easily the best Scrooge yet.
As escapism that’s also all-too-pertinent, with the prettiest staging and the loveliest music, this production really is the crème de la crème of traditional Christmas Carols.
Eccleston, who really does feel born to play the central role, is ably supported by an ensemble that features several returning cast members.
I struggle to think of another show that captures the Christmas spirit as perfectly as this one does.

cn.t: Critics praise this Old Vic tradition as its strongest outing yet, with Christopher Eccleston delivering a superb Scrooge whose hard-won redemption anchors Jack Thorne's compassionate adaptation and Matthew Warchus' beautifully staged production.
